draft.title: Fieldwork and primary data
card: Fieldwork is the study of a place by going there. Data that a geographer collects first-hand is called primary data.
Observations record what you see, such as land use or signs of erosion. Measurements record amounts with tools, such as stream width, wind speed or pedestrian counts.
A survey asks many people the same set of questions, so answers can be compared. An interview asks fewer people, in more depth, about their views and experiences.
Primary data suits a question about a particular place that no one has studied. Geographers plan the sites, tools and timing first so the data is fair and can be repeated.
draft.remember: Primary data is collected first-hand by the geographer, in the field.

a.q: Which of these is an example of primary data?
opts: A student counts cyclists passing a bridge in one hour
A student uses census figures on how people travel to work
A student reads a council report on cycling numbers
A student copies rainfall records from a weather website
a.why: The student collected the cyclist count first-hand by standing at the site. The other three use information that someone else already collected, so they are not primary data.
a.clue: Who collected the data: the student or someone else?

b.q: Kai is studying how locals feel about a new beachfront walkway in Port Macquarie. He wants detailed views from a few long-term residents. Which method suits this best?
opts: Interviews with a small number of residents
A tally of walkers at one spot over an hour
Measuring the width of the walkway with a tape
Observing the walkway's surface and signs of wear
b.why: Interviews collect fewer people's views in depth, which is what Kai wants. A tally, measurements and observations are primary data too, but they record what is there or how many, not what people think.
b.clue: Which method asks people about their views in depth?

a.best: A student counts cyclists passing a bridge in one hour

b.best: Interviews with a small number of residents

problems.detail: The remember line says primary data is collected 'in the field', but the card only says it is data a geographer collects first-hand. Primary data such as a phone interview or an online survey can be collected away from the site, so the line ties primary data to fieldwork more tightly than the card does.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, with one clear right answer each. One minor issue: the remember line says primary data is collected 'in the field', which is narrower than the card's definition of first-hand data.
